- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect market resilience or mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 70+ to 75+), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive — cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or use lagged mean.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 75+ → 70–72), model often fails to correct — apply downward bias in next 5–7 days if sentiment is weak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate when sentiment is volatile or mixed — add 0.5–1.5% buffer if sentiment swings >0.3 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated high positive values followed by low prices, model often fails to anticipate drop — apply downward correction in 10–15 day window.
